payload.excerpt: Build a wedding table setting piece by piece, from charger and cutlery to glassware, napkin and name card, then see how seven themes change the same pieces and what to ask a venue abroad.
key_takeaways: A place setting is built from the menu, with cutlery laid in order of use from the outside in and nothing set that will not be used.
Forks sit to the left, knives and spoons to the right, glasses above the knives, and dessert cutlery either above the plate or brought out with dessert.

A theme lives in the finish of each piece, not in adding more, and the seven looks below are classic and formal, pared back, garden and romantic, coastal, country estate, winter and candlelit, and playful and retro.
For a destination wedding, ask the venue what tableware it holds and what must be hired in, then judge the whole setting at a mock-up.

faq.q: Which side does the bread plate go on?
faq.a: The bread plate sits to the upper left of the setting, above the forks. The butter knife rests across it with the blade facing inward toward the diner.

faq.q: How many glasses does each guest need?
faq.a: At a less formal dinner, a water glass plus one or perhaps two wine glasses to its right. At a formal dinner with a different wine for each course, there is a glass for each, cascading to the right. Add a coupe or flute if the toasts call for one.

faq.q: Where does the dessert cutlery go?
faq.a: Either above the plate for the whole meal, with the fork's handle pointing left and the spoon above it, handle pointing right, or brought out with dessert.

faq.q: Should the napkin go on the plate or to the left?
faq.a: Either is correct: to the left of the forks or in the centre of the charger. Choose by look. A napkin on the charger shows off a fold or a name card; one to the left leaves the plate clear.

faq.q: Do we need chargers at a wedding?
faq.a: No. A charger plate may be used or left out. It adds formality and colour, so it suits a plated dinner and a classic theme more than a shared table.

faq.q: Can a venue abroad supply all the tableware?
faq.a: That depends on the venue. Ask what tableware, glassware and linen it holds, for how many guests, and what would need to be hired in, then get the answers in writing and see the pieces laid at a mock-up before you commit.
